nodes.label: Per-Category Tier Rubric
nodes.rationale: User criteria per category define the crown (3-5/page), star (7-9/page) and minimum tiers; exemptions exist for special tools (Pi-hole-style network tools, legendary archival indexes, private trackers, abandonware, academic archives).

nodes.label: FMHY Ordering Principle
nodes.rationale: FMHY orders entries by trust: entries at the top of a section are the most trusted and highest quality, quality decreases further down, and stars follow the same trend; curation must preserve this ordering.

nodes.label: ThemeHandler (Singleton)
nodes.rationale: Singleton manages all theme state; reads the effective mode from VitePress's dark class instead of managing it, so palettes apply on every page including the home page where no sidebar components mount.

nodes.label: applyTheme
nodes.source_location: state.ts, How applyTheme() Works section line 124

nodes.label: ColorPicker.vue
nodes.rationale: When a theme omits brand colors, the handler removes inline brand variables so the ColorPicker stylesheet takes priority; theme-changed-apply-colors lets the picker reapply after theme switches.

nodes.label: VitePress native appearance toggle
nodes.rationale: Display mode is managed entirely by VitePress (HTML class, persistence, system preference); the theme engine only reads it. The custom theme mode selector and AMOLED support were removed; display mode is now the native VitePress light/dark toggle (appearance: true).

nodes.label: Modes-Themes Orthogonality Principle
nodes.rationale: Key principle: Modes and themes are orthogonal. Switching from light to dark mode doesn't change your theme. Switching your theme doesn't change your mode. The theme system is built around two independent concepts: display modes and themes.

nodes.label: vitepress-theme-name persistence key
nodes.rationale: localStorage key storing the active theme name (e.g. catppuccin, color-swarm). The display mode is persisted separately by VitePress under its own key.

nodes.label: CSS variables mapping
nodes.rationale: ModeColors fields map to VitePress CSS variables: brand -> --vp-c-brand-*, bg -> --vp-c-bg, bgAlt -> --vp-c-bg-alt, bgElv -> --vp-c-bg-elv, text -> --vp-c-text-*, button -> --vp-button-*, customBlock -> --vp-custom-block-{type}-*, plus --vp-c-selection-bg, --vp-home-hero-*, --vp-font-family-*, --vp-border-radius, --vp-spacing-*, --vp-theme-logo.

nodes.label: Theme creation workflow
nodes.source_location: How to Create a New Theme section line 182
nodes.rationale: Steps: create configs/theme-<name>.ts with a Theme object, register it in themeRegistry in configs/registry.ts; the theme then automatically appears in the ColorPicker sidebar as a preset circle. Tips: omit brand to let ColorPicker control accents, omit text for VitePress defaults, add preview for a recognizable circle (gradient fallback from brand colors), use customProperties for arbitrary CSS variables.

nodes.label: theme-changed-apply-colors event
nodes.rationale: Custom event dispatched by the handler after a theme switch; ColorPicker listens for it to reapply its color selection when the new theme doesn't define brand colors. notifyColorPicker() must be called in setTheme() or colors won't update.

nodes.label: color-* dynamic themes
nodes.source_location: Theme Registry section line 177, ColorPicker Integration section line 337
nodes.rationale: ColorPicker generates a Theme object from predefined color palettes (swarm, meadow, etc.) and registers it at runtime as themeRegistry['color-<name>'] (e.g. color-swarm, color-meadow).

nodes.label: Brand color interaction
nodes.rationale: When a theme defines brand colors they are set as inline CSS variables and override anything ColorPicker sets; when a theme omits brand, the handler removes inline brand variables and ColorPicker's stylesheet takes priority.

nodes.label: Theme Registry (registry.ts)
nodes.rationale: Plain object mapping names to Theme objects. The ColorPicker dynamically registers generated color themes (e.g. color-swarm) at runtime.

nodes.label: Mode Sync (MutationObserver)
nodes.source_location: Mechanism: observes VitePress's dark class on <html> via a MutationObserver set up in boot() on the client only, re-applying the active theme palette whenever VitePress flips the class.

nodes.label: Theme Persistence (vitepress-theme-name)
nodes.source_location: Mechanism: active theme name persisted under the localStorage key vitepress-theme-name; display mode is persisted separately by VitePress under vitepress-theme-appearance.

nodes.label: theme-changed-apply-colors Event
nodes.source_location: Mechanism: custom event dispatched by the handler after a theme switch; ColorPicker listens to reapply its color selection when the new theme does not define brand colors.

nodes.label: VitePress (Display Mode Owner)
nodes.source_location: VitePress owns the display mode (appearance: true); the theme engine only reads it.

nodes.label: The Top-Tier Only
nodes.rationale: Site-wide rule: each category is strictly capped at 20 entries so users only get the best content, avoiding the noise and low-quality entries of larger wikis.

nodes.label: icon-transformer.ts
nodes.rationale: crown to crown-icon mapping was added here as the user's preferred approach for the crown tier marker; the crown icon was verified to exist in @iconify-json/twemoji.

nodes.label: Markdown Emoji Transformation
nodes.rationale: Raw Unicode emojis in markdown text and headings are converted into optimized Iconify/Twemoji components with precise regex and token replacement.

nodes.label: Modes/Themes Orthogonality
nodes.rationale: Modes and themes are orthogonal: switching light/dark mode does not change the theme and vice versa; the display mode is owned entirely by VitePress (appearance: true) and the theme engine only reads it.

nodes.label: Big Wiki Noise Problem
nodes.rationale: Big free media wikis (FMHY, r/Piracy, Awesome, Wotaku.wiki, EverythingMoe) mix good and bad, active and dead, safe and risky resources; bitindex solves this by curating only the best of the best with a strict 20-entry cap per section.
